title: Pastitsio
subtitle: Greek baked pasta with spiced meat sauce and bechamel
excerpt: The great Greek baked pasta: tubes of macaroni layered with a cinnamon-scented lamb and tomato sauce, topped with a thick bechamel crust, baked until golden and set. A celebration dish that feeds a crowd and tastes better the next day.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pastitsio is the Greek answer to lasagne: a baked pasta dish with meat sauce and a thick bechamel, but constructed in a different fashion and with a distinctly different flavour. The defining characteristic is the use of ground cinnamon and allspice in the meat sauce, spices introduced through centuries of Ottoman culinary influence on Greek cooking. The dish takes its name from the Italian pasticcio (mixed-up, a mess), reflecting the shared Mediterranean baking tradition of mixed pasta and meat layers under a cream sauce. Pastitsio is a celebration dish, made for Easter, name days, and large family gatherings. It sets into a firm, sliceable block once cooled; it is often considered to taste better on the second day after the layers have had time to meld.

recipeTools.notes: A deep 30 x 20 cm baking tin.

content.text: The cinnamon is not a background note; it should be assertively present. The bechamel must be thick enough to hold the pasta layer below it; a runny bechamel produces a sunken, wet top. Allow the pastitsio to cool for at least 15 minutes before cutting so the layers set and the portions hold their shape.

items.preparation: penne or ziti; cooked al dente
grated; half for the bechamel, half for the top

content.text: Make the meat sauce: heat the olive oil in a large pan and brown the lamb mince in batches until well coloured. Remove. Fry the onion for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, cinnamon, allspice, and oregano and cook for 1 minute. Return the mince. Add the tinned tomatoes and 150 ml water. Simmer for 25 minutes until thick. Season.

Make the bechamel: melt the butter in a saucepan. Add the flour and cook, stirring, for 1 minute. Gradually add the warm milk, whisking continuously until thick and smooth. Cook for 5 minutes. Remove from the heat, stir in half the parmesan, and season. Cool for 5 minutes then beat in the eggs.

Heat the oven to 180 C (160 C fan). Spread half the pasta in the base of a 30 x 20 cm baking tin. Spread the meat sauce evenly over the pasta. Cover with the remaining pasta. Pour the bechamel over the top, spreading evenly. Scatter with the remaining parmesan. Bake for 45 to 50 minutes until golden brown and set. Rest for 15 minutes before cutting into squares.
